name: Chandranshu Sinha
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, EkAnek Networks (Foxy beauty-shopping app); co-founder of OfBusiness
profile: Indian technologist who co-founded B2B commerce and lending unicorn OfBusiness (OFB Tech), where he headed products. In 2018 he co-founded EkAnek Networks, which runs Foxy, an artist-led online shopping platform for beauty, grooming and personal care, where he serves as CTO.
interesting_fact: After helping build OfBusiness, he left to co-found Foxy (EkAnek Networks, founded 2018) alongside Kartik Sheth, Nikhil Gilani and Sachin Singhal.
notes: No longer listed on OfBusiness's current team page (https://www.ofbusiness.com/about/team?tab=team); best route is via Foxy/EkAnek. Background reportedly IIT Kharagpur, DevFactory and Trilogy, but that comes from a single weak source (CrazyEngineers), so it is not used as a fact. Low public profile.

name: Grant LaFontaine
profile: Maine-raised consumer-tech product executive who co-founded Whatnot with Logan Head in 2019. It went through Y Combinator's Winter 2020 batch, starting with Funko Pops before expanding into trading cards, fashion and more. Whatnot is now a leading US live-stream shopping platform, reported by Fortune at a $20B valuation in 2026.
interesting_fact: While raising money, the founders pitched hundreds of investors and logged each rejection in a spreadsheet, but stopped updating it at 100 rows because they were too 'demoralized'. Whatnot's first livestream, which LaFontaine hosted, sold out in about 2.5 hours.
deep_cut_fact: He opened an eBay store in fourth grade, selling Pokemon cards with friends in Maine. His first online sale was a holographic Chansey card, the sale that hooked him as both a collector and a seller.
notes: Could not verify a current Whatnot press email in this session. 2022 Business Wire releases reportedly listed Moxie PR (whatnot@moxiegrouppr.com) as the agency, but I could not open those pages to confirm, so it is not listed as a contact. Has appeared on the a16z and Masters of Scale podcasts.

name: Chaitanya Kanojia
current_role: Co-founder of Starry (fixed-wireless broadband); stepped down as CEO in June 2023 and was reported to stay on the board
profile: Chaitanya 'Chet' Kanojia is a Boston-area serial telecom/media entrepreneur. He ran Navic Networks, an advanced TV advertising firm Microsoft acquired in 2008. He then founded Aereo, a cloud-antenna TV service, followed by Starry, a fixed-wireless home internet provider founded around 2014 that listed via SPAC in 2022. He handed Starry's CEO role to COO Alex Moulle-Berteaux in June 2023.
interesting_fact: His earlier startup Aereo, which put an over-the-air TV antenna and DVR in the cloud, took its fight with broadcasters all the way to the US Supreme Court. He then built Starry as his next attempt to disrupt incumbent networks.
deep_cut_fact: Some of his investors at FirstMark have known him for about 20 years. He told TechCrunch he wanted backers who had 'seen that movie', meaning stayed with a company from seed stage all the way to IPO.
notes: Starry went through Chapter 11 in 2023 and was taken private; avoid this topic in outreach. In the 2023 transition post he said he wanted to dedicate more time to his family. His current activity is unclear. Highly relevant to a telecom/infrastructure podcast.
